speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly what happens when you wake up frightened? Do you scream, kick, or look terrified, and can you remember the dream afterward?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do these frightening episodes occur during the night or very early in the morning, and do you ever recall having a nightmare about them?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder. The history of recurrent distressing dreams leading to awakening, followed by rapid return to full alertness and detailed recall, is characteristic of this condition rather than sleep terrors. REQUEST TEST: Pediatric Sleep Diary (2 weeks). REQUEST IMAGES: Normal Pediatric Brain MRI (for baseline).
